speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me if this onset was sudden or gradual, and do you notice any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant trauma from the jersey pull. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and is there significant bruising or a deformity to the finger now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion Fracture of the Extensor Tendon at the Distal Interphalangeal Joint).

The history of forced flexion of an extended finger, combined with the inability to actively extend the distal interphalangeal joint, is classic for this injury. Please confirm if you can actively extend the tip of the finger when the other fingers are extended, and if so, I will proceed to imaging.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
